full_judgment: 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that Abdul Khaleque Munshi, the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners, as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title in the suit property and for a declaration that the proceedings before the concerned Revenue Officer are illegal and without jurisdiction in the 4th Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 383 of 1983, contending inter alia that the suit property appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 107 in C.S. Plot 565 comprising an area of 80.68 acres in mouza Tejkunipara within P.S. Keraniganj, now Gulshan, Dhaka originally belonged to Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate the S. khattari urordingly pareas in the name of Kumai Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. As the laid was a marshy land under deep water it was recorded in the C.S. khatian as 'Beel Bhumr. Abdul Khaleque Munshi being the neighboring owner of some other land started filling earth at his own cost during the years 1927-1936 as a result of which land became fit for cultivation and he grew boro paddy therein. It has been stated that the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate having found Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamders in possession of the suit land demanded rent from Abdul Khaleque Munshi and he agreed to pay rent whereupon between 1936-1947, the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate settled 52.17 acres of land by different pattan names on different dates and prepared C.S. B khatian in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamdars and realised rent from them by entering their names in the Tenants' Register No. II, showing the area of land settled and the rate of jama and other charges but Abdul Khaleque Munshi refused to pay rent to the Bhawal. Raj Court of Wards Estate as owner of 28.51 acres of land on the ground that he had been possessing the same on the basis of adverse possession by making it fit for cultivation at his own cost and exertions. As Torab and others illegally cut and took away boro paddy grown by him, Abdul Khaleque Munshi filed a criminal case against those trespassers under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The learned SDO and the appellate Court found the said Abdul Khaleque Munshi in possession of 80.68 acres of land and restrained the trespassers by way of injunction from entering into the case land. Thereafter Torab Ali and 91 others filed a suit for declaration of title against Abdul Khaleque Munshi in the 1st Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 89 of 1962. In the said suit the learned Subordinate Judge found Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin as borgaders under the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin filed Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 in the Court of the District Judge, Dhaka and the learned Additional District Judge, who heard the said appeal, allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment of the trial court on the finding that Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin have right title, interest and possession in the land of CS Plot No. 565. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, Abdul Khaleque Munshi, son of Abdul Hakim, Torab Ali and 90 others filed Second Appeal No. 685 of 1970 before the High Court Division but the said appeal was also dismissed and the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 were affirmed. Against the aforesaid judgment of the High Court Division, Abdul Khaleque Munshi , Son of Abdul Hakim and 91 others, who were the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962, filed CPLA No 84 of 1974 before the Appellate Division but were unsuccessful. Eventually 14.16 acres of land out of the aforesaid 80.68 acres of land in CS Plot No. 565 was acquired by the Rajuk in Land Acquisition Case No. 55 of 1958-59 and compensation was assessed in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamder Amiruddin. As the compensation assessed by the Collector was inadequate, plaintiffs Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin filed Arbitration Case No. 248 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka who ultimately assessed compensation at Tk. 347760/00 in place of Tk. 46368/00 as assessed by the Collector. Against the aforesaid judgment and order the Government filed 2nd Appeal No. 169 of 1970, which was subsequently converted into Civil Revision No. 807 of 1993 before the High Court Division, to reduce the amount of compensation. The Government thus recognized and accepted the title of the plaintiff Abdul Khaleque Munshi in the suit land. In the meantime, RS operation in respect of the land of 80.68 acres along with other lands started. In the Bujarat stage of RS operation plaintiff Abdul Khaleque Munshi got the land of 80.68 acres recorded in his name and in the name of his benamder and transferees but at the attestation stage the Government and other persons, including the principal defendants, filed a dispute case claiming title in 80.68 acres of land. Most of the defendants are either the heirs and heiresses or transferees of the 92 plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962 in the 1st. Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. It was alleged that not only the defendants have got no legal claim or title in the suit land but also their claim is barred by the principle of resjudicata in view of the decision in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 89 of 1962 and Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964. It has been further alleged that the settlement officer of the basis of some false and fabricated documents and in deference to the decision of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962, Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 and Second Appeal No. 685 of 1970 and CPLA No. 84 of 1974, recognised the claim of the defendants and illegally passed order for recording the names of the defendants in the RS khatian in respect of 80.68 acres of land, including 17.3067 acres in the name of transposed plaintiff Nos. 2-12 as shown in schedule 'B' and .4164 acres of land in the name of pro-forma defendant No. 128 as shown in schedule 'C' to the plaint. The land measuring 1.4750 acres out of 52.17 acres has not been recorded the name of pro-forma defendant Nos. 129 and 130, and it has been wrongly shown as vest-ed property. It has been further alleged that no land having vested in the Government, it cannot claim any title thereto. The defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land measuring 80.68 acres and the claim of the defendants and the orders of the settlement officials during the RS operation recording the suit land in the names of the defendants are wrong and hence the suit for declaration of title in the suit land.
